CFML Language Reference: Functions

IsQuery

Returns YES if the value is a query object, whether it came from CFQUERY, another tag that returns a query (such as CFDIRECTORY or CFPOP), or QueryNew.

Category

Decision functions

Syntax

IsQuery(value)

Parameters

value
Any value.

Returns

YES or NO.

Usage

Custom tags often use IsQuery to check that an attribute passed in really is a query before looping over it.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFQUERY NAME="GetDepts" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">
SELECT Dept_Name FROM Departments
</CFQUERY>
<CFSET Made = QueryNew("Name, Price")>
<CFSET List = ValueList(GetDepts.Dept_Name)>
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TH>Variable</TH><TH>IsQuery</TH></TR>
<CFOUTPUT>
<TR><TD>GetDepts (CFQUERY)</TD><TD>#IsQuery(GetDepts)#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>Made (QueryNew)</TD><TD>#IsQuery(Made)#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>List: #List#</TD><TD>#IsQuery(List)#</TD></TR>
</CFOUTPUT>
</TABLE>

See also

QueryNew, CFQUERY, IsStruct, IsArray
